cards.title: Guided first run opens as a four-screen modal over the app
cards.user_does: Launches Kolux for the first time on a fresh profile.
cards.user_sees: A centred card over a dimmed, lightly blurred app with the Kolux mark, a row of four progress bars plus a counter giving the current position out of four, a large heading and one-line subheading for the current screen, a scrollable body, and a footer with the screen's actions.
rules: Screens run in a fixed order: welcome, connect an AI, your work, choose a kit.
The current bar is wider and solid, finished bars are mid-tone, later bars are faint; hovering a bar shows that screen's heading as a tooltip.

Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on Mac) triggers the screen's primary action unless focus is in a text field or an IME composition is in progress; it does nothing while the primary action is disabled. The shortcut is fixed, not rebindable.
The footer shows Back only from screen 2 on; the primary button carries a small modifier + Return chip; a secondary action, when present, sits on the left.
A thin strip along the top edge stays draggable so the window can still be moved.
While the starter-kit setup dialog is open, the wizard hides itself but keeps its state, then reappears when that dialog closes.
The card caps at roughly 860 px wide and 880 px tall and shrinks with the window.
acceptance: Fresh profile → wizard shows screen 1 and the counter reads one out of four.
Press Ctrl+Enter on screen 1 → advances to screen 2; press it while typing in a field → nothing happens.
On screen 1 there is no Back button; on screen 2 Back returns to screen 1.

cards.title: Welcome screen shows three AIs working side by side
cards.user_does: Reads the first screen and clicks 'Get started'.
cards.user_sees: A heading that says several AIs can work on the user's own files at once, and three small tiles, one per AI (Claude, Codex, Grok), each with a short activity label and a pulsing status dot.
rules: The status-dot pulse only animates when the system does not ask for reduced motion.
All three tiles always render.
'Get started' is always enabled and moves to screen 2.
acceptance: Turn on reduced motion → the three tiles render with still dots.
Click 'Get started' → screen 2 appears and progress is saved.

cards.title: Connect an AI screen gates Continue on at least one connection
cards.user_does: Signs in to one AI provider from the cards on screen 2, or clicks 'I'll do this later'.
cards.user_sees: The same provider Connect cards used elsewhere in the app, under a subheading that promises sign-in on an existing plan with no terminal. Continue stays disabled until any provider shows as connected.
rules: Continue is enabled as soon as any provider reports connected.
'I'll do this later' advances to screen 3 without a connection.
The first time any AI becomes connected, a local first-AI-connected milestone is stamped (see the milestones card).
acceptance: No provider connected → Continue disabled; 'I'll do this later' moves on.
Connect one provider → Continue becomes enabled without leaving the screen.

cards.title: Your work screen: pick a folder or try sample data
cards.user_does: On screen 3 clicks 'Pick a folder', or chooses one of the sample datasets and clicks Continue ('Try with sample data').
cards.user_sees: Two paths separated by an 'or': a folder picker that leaves the wizard for the normal Add Project flow, and a list of sample cards (icon beside the title) with the spreadsheet-analysis sample preselected.
rules: Only starter kits that ship sample data appear as samples; the default is the spreadsheet-analysis kit.
Continue builds the chosen sample as a workspace; while it loads, Continue shows busy and is disabled.
If the sample cannot be built, the wizard stays on screen 3 and no workspace is set.
Building the sample also closes the launch-agents modal that would normally pop open for a new workspace, and preselects the matching kit on screen 4.
Pick a folder marks onboarding completed and hands off to Add Project; the wizard does not return.
acceptance: Open screen 3 → the spreadsheet sample is preselected.
Continue with a sample → screen 4 opens with that sample's kit already selected and no extra launch modal on screen.
Pick a folder → wizard closes as completed and the Add Project dialog opens.

cards.title: Choose a starter kit screen launches a kit or a plain session
cards.user_does: On screen 4 picks a kit card and clicks 'Start kit', or clicks 'Just open a session'; may flip the done-notification switch.
cards.user_sees: Kit cards with their seat roles, a switch to be pinged when an AI finishes (on by default), and either an immediate launch or the kit setup dialog.
rules: The kit implied by the chosen sample is preselected; otherwise the first kit in the catalogue.

'Start kit' launches at once, without the setup dialog, only when the sample workspace already fills every required input and an agent is available; otherwise the kit setup dialog opens (no workspace yet, a real folder, or no agent).
'Just open a session' launches one empty-prompt session with the first available agent in the shared checkout; with no agent or no workspace it does nothing and onboarding stays open.
The ping switch is the app-wide notifications setting, so changing it here changes it everywhere.
A successful launch by either path marks onboarding completed and starts the grid tour.
acceptance: Sample workspace + available agent → 'Start kit' launches without a dialog and the wizard closes.
No agent installed → 'Start kit' opens the setup dialog; 'Just open a session' does nothing.
Turn the ping switch off → the notifications setting is off in Settings.

cards.title: Leaving the wizard asks for confirmation and says how to come back
cards.user_does: Presses Escape, or clicks outside the wizard card.
cards.user_sees: A small confirmation dialog asking whether to skip setup, telling the user where in Help they can resume, with 'Skip' and 'No, keep going'.
rules: Only a primary-button click outside every onboarding surface asks; clicks inside the card, inside nested dialogs or dropdown menus (such as the sound picker), and non-primary clicks are ignored.
Escape while the confirmation is already open does not stack a second one.
Skip closes onboarding as dismissed: no tour starts, and the sidebar checklist is marked dismissed.
'No, keep going' returns to the same screen.
acceptance: Press Escape on screen 2 → confirmation appears; 'No, keep going' → still on screen 2.
Right-click outside the card → nothing happens.
Skip → wizard closes and no tour appears.

cards.title: Wizard progress and outcome persist; a failed save can be retried
cards.user_does: Moves through screens, quits midway, or finishes.
cards.user_sees: On relaunch the wizard resumes at the screen reached; after finishing or skipping it does not come back. If saving the close fails, an error toast says progress could not be saved and the user can try again.
rules: Each forward step saves the last completed screen; the move happens even if that save fails.
Closing records when it closed and whether it was completed or dismissed; a completed close records the final screen as done.
Closing is latched: a second close while the first is in flight does nothing; a failed save releases the latch so the user can retry.
A completed close asks the star prompt to show its onboarding-completed toast on the next tick.
acceptance: Advance to screen 3, quit, relaunch → wizard opens on screen 3.
Finish via 'Just open a session', relaunch → no wizard.
Make the save fail on close → error toast; clicking the action again retries.
cards.compat: Onboarding state in the profile (flow version, closed time, outcome completed or dismissed, last completed screen, checklist booleans, milestone times) is a data category the importer must carry.

cards.title: Only new profiles see the wizard; older progress is mapped forward
cards.user_does: Updates Kolux from an older version, or starts with an existing profile.
cards.user_sees: Existing users are never forced through the new wizard; someone mid-way through an older version resumes at the equivalent screen or restarts at screen 1.
rules: A profile with no onboarding record at all counts as already completed.
Progress from the version that had a view-choice screen after welcome shifts back one slot past it; progress from the version without it is kept as is.
Any open progress from the older five-step wizard restarts at screen 1, even if it was dismissed.
Older versions keep their own fallbacks (completed with enough steps → final screen; in-progress capped).
Progress is clamped to the four screens; the stored version is bumped to the current one on load.
A missing closed time is recovered when an outcome exists.
acceptance: Load a profile with no onboarding block → no wizard.
Load progress saved past the old view-choice screen → wizard resumes on the same visible screen.
Load open progress from the five-step wizard → wizard starts at screen 1.
cards.compat: The importer must carry onboarding progress and outcome so imported users are not re-onboarded.

cards.title: Reopen the wizard from the sidebar Help menu
cards.user_does: Opens the sidebar help menu and clicks 'Onboarding'.
cards.user_sees: The guided first run opens again from screen 1.
rules: Reopening clears the closed time, outcome and progress but keeps the rest of the checklist state; only the dismissed mark is cleared.
Clicks within half a second of each other count once.
acceptance: Finish onboarding, then click 'Onboarding' in the help menu → wizard shows screen 1 again.
Double-click the item quickly → wizard opens once.

cards.title: First folder added after onboarding auto-starts the default agent
cards.user_does: Adds a first project folder right after onboarding (via 'Pick a folder', or after skipping before any project existed).
cards.user_sees: A session with the user's saved default agent opens in that folder without further clicks.
rules: Uses the saved default agent; if the default is a blank terminal, a blank terminal opens; an automatic default does not guess an agent.
Chat-style defaults open as chat, terminal defaults as terminal.
Applies after a skipped run only if no project had been added yet; never when a project already existed or onboarding itself already added one.
acceptance: Default agent set, skip onboarding with no projects, add a folder → that agent starts in it.
Add a second project later → no automatic agent.

cards.title: First-success milestones are stamped locally and show in diagnostics
cards.user_does: Connects a first AI, launches a first kit, opens first results; later copies terminal diagnostics.
cards.user_sees: Nothing during use; the copied diagnostics include when each first milestone happened.
rules: Three milestones: first AI connected, first kit launched, first results opened.
Each is written once, the first time it happens, and never overwritten; a missing value counts as not yet.
Milestones never leave the machine.
acceptance: Connect an AI twice → the milestone keeps the first time.
Copy terminal diagnostics after a kit launch → the kit-launched time is listed.
cards.compat: Milestone timestamps are part of the onboarding data the importer must carry.

cards.title: Grid tour runs once after the first run finishes
cards.user_does: Finishes onboarding by launching a kit or a plain session.
cards.user_sees: A three-stop callout tour on the live grid: what a session is, where its status shows (spinning, yellow, green), and where to collect results.
rules: Starts only after a kit or plain-session finish, and only once; skip and folder-picker finishes do not start it.
Uses the same overlay, skip and progress rules as every contextual tour.
acceptance: Finish with 'Just open a session' → tour points at the terminal, then the sidebar, then the kit results.
Skip onboarding → no tour.

cards.title: Newcomer setup checklist (four plain first-success items)
cards.user_does: Opens the setup checklist as a newcomer.
cards.user_sees: Intended: a short checklist of connect an AI, run a kit, open results, run on your own file, with a one-time toast when all four are done.
rules: Items derive from connection state and the milestones; the list counts as done only when ready and all four are ticked.
The all-done toast fires once per profile, not per launch, and not on re-renders.

Gate defect at 0.15.0: the checklist only appears for profiles on onboarding flow version 5, but every profile is migrated to version 7 on load, so nobody sees it; the generic eight-step setup guide shows instead.
The checklist always points at the first unticked item in a fixed order (connect an AI, run a kit, open results, run on your own file); once all four are ticked there is no next item.
acceptance: If built: a new profile that finishes onboarding sees the four-item list; completing all four shows one toast that never repeats.
cards.decision: H: default build. It is the newcomer path the business frame designed; at 0.15.0 it is unreachable only because of a version-gate mismatch.

cards.title: Setup Guide dialog with a progress ring and step list
cards.user_does: Opens Help › 'Getting Started with Kolux', the sidebar checklist entry, or 'Milestones' in the sidebar help menu.
cards.user_sees: A dialog with a progress ring (core steps done of total), a step list grouped into a Setup section followed by a numbered parallel-work section, and the selected step's action on the right; an eye-off button hides the checklist from the sidebar.
rules: Eight steps: Multi-task, Use Kolux's browser, notifications, default agent, Enable Kolux CLI, Connect integrations, Automate workspace setup, Start work in multiple repos.
Opens on the first incomplete step, Setup section first, then parallel work; a caller can ask for a specific step and the guide moves on once that step completes.
The 'Milestones' help-menu item only appears while core steps are incomplete and carries a small progress ring.
Content stays mounted through the close animation; reopening during that time cancels the unmount.
Step names and descriptions exist in English and Korean.
acceptance: Open from Help → first incomplete step is selected.
Complete every core step → 'Milestones' disappears from the help menu.
Close and reopen quickly → no flicker of empty content.

cards.title: Setup Guide steps complete from real state, not from clicks
cards.user_does: Works normally; the guide ticks steps off as things become true.
cards.user_sees: Ticks appear only when the underlying thing exists.
rules: Multi-task: done once a real non-main workspace exists beyond the main checkout; a placeholder or two main checkouts do not count.
Browser: done once a non-blank page has been viewed.
Multiple repos: done from the durable count of git projects (two or more).
Integrations: done when any supported provider is connected, not while checks are pending.
CLI and capabilities: done only when required skills and permissions are ready; an unavailable desktop-control capability never blocks it; starting setup alone does not count.
Workspace setup script: readiness resets when inputs change, ignores late older results, and a failed probe settles as no script.
Old profiles that had finished the earlier steps, or had dismissed the sidebar checklist, count as legacy-complete everywhere; a failed status read is not treated as completion.
A retired split-terminal step no longer counts toward progress.
acceptance: Only the main checkout exists → Multi-task not ticked; create one workspace → ticked.
Open a blank browser tab → Browser not ticked; load a page → ticked.

cards.title: Setup Guide step actions for workspaces, notifications and default agent
cards.user_does: Uses the action panel of a selected step.
cards.user_sees: Multi-task opens the new-workspace composer with a short tour; notifications shows sound choices and, on macOS, a permission card; default agent shows an agent picker with a collapsible list of fallback agents; the setup-script step offers to automate workspace setup.
rules: Actions that need a project first ask for one; workspace creation uses the active git project, else the first git project; folders without git never qualify.
A stale composer request after close and reopen is ignored; tour retries only fire on the expected screen.

The macOS permission card stays hidden until the delivery check returns: delivered means enabled, pending means awaiting, a first rejection reads as an unanswered dialog, a later rejection as blocked; it is hidden where notifications are unsupported.
No volume slider is shown for non-system sounds; the old per-source notification switches are gone.
The fallback-agents list sits behind a summary toggle whose label reads show while collapsed and hide while expanded.
acceptance: Only a non-git folder added → Multi-task asks for a git project.
macOS, notifications previously denied → card reads as blocked.

cards.title: Enable Kolux CLI step installs the CLI and agent skills
cards.user_does: Selects the capabilities to set up (CLI, skills such as orchestration and browser use) and runs setup.
cards.user_sees: A checklist of capabilities with missing ones preselected and ready ones unchecked, an explanation of CLI registration before install, a small inline terminal with the install command already typed at its prompt, waiting for the user to press Enter, and a copyable command.
rules: Every setup item defaults on so first-launch setup is ready to run.
Selected skills install through one combined command; selecting only orchestration never touches browser or desktop-control setup.
On Windows with WSL, commands run through the chosen WSL distro; if that runtime needs repair they fall back to the host, and the runtime chosen at start is kept for the run.
A copied command is shaped for the target shell; failure to copy warns.
If PATH cannot be read from the registry, it warns without changing PATH.
On macOS a Full Disk Access prompt appears only for statuses the user can act on, refreshes when Kolux regains focus, opens the system setting, and never appears on other systems.
Clearing every selection clears the setup markers.

The inline setup terminal opens in the user's shell, waits until a prompt is visible (or, when no prompt text can be read, until the terminal has been up briefly), then types the setup command without running it; a short note under it says to press Enter.
It gives up waiting for the prompt after a capped number of checks (about fifty) instead of polling forever.

If the shell the terminal ends up in changes, for example from a WSL distro to the host, the command is re-shaped for that shell and typed again; the same command is never typed twice into the same terminal.
When the setup shell exits, installed skills are re-detected so the step can tick off; exit results from any other terminal are ignored.
When the setup panel disappears, its terminal is closed so no installer keeps running out of sight.
acceptance: CLI installed but skills missing → only skills preselected.
WSL distro broken → setup runs on the Windows host.
Windows → no Full Disk Access prompt.

Open the CLI step → the inline terminal shows the install command at the prompt, not yet run; press Enter → it runs, and when the shell exits the step re-checks and ticks off if the skills are now installed.

cards.title: Connect integrations step: GitHub review and tasks
cards.user_does: Connects GitHub from the Connect integrations step.
cards.user_sees: A review step and a task-source step; once GitHub is connected both resolve and the task step collapses to a summary listing the connected source.
rules: The review step is active first and the task step waits, collapsed but openable.
A connected code host completes the task step only after review is connected and tracker checks have settled.
Cached sign-in is not shown as connected while checks are stale or errored; a failed token sign-in is not review-ready.
Rebuild keeps GitHub only (see the cut card for other providers).
acceptance: Nothing connected → review active, tasks upcoming.
Connect GitHub → both steps done and GitHub listed in the summary.

cards.title: Non-GitHub providers in the setup guide and feature wall
cards.user_does: Would connect GitLab, Linear or Jira from the integrations step or the Tasks stop of Explore Kolux.
cards.user_sees: Provider rows and tracker-first ordering for those services.
rules: Trackers were listed before code hosts; a tracker connected first completed the task step on its own.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea, Jira and Linear are dropped by owner (table 1b); GitHub stays. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Sidebar onboarding checklist entry
cards.user_does: Sees a checklist entry in the left sidebar after onboarding; clicks it or picks 'Hide from sidebar'.
cards.user_sees: A compact entry with progress that opens the Setup Guide, and a hide option.
rules: Hiding persists.
On every load the entry counts as dismissed once onboarding has ever closed, so in practice it only shows in the session in which onboarding closed.
The newcomer variant is used only for newcomer profiles (unreachable, see the newcomer checklist card).
A finished setup never makes the entry flash into view while capability checks are still loading.
Only an explicit hide counts as hidden when saved state loads.
acceptance: Finish onboarding → entry visible; relaunch → entry gone.
'Hide from sidebar' → entry gone and stays gone.
Relaunch with every step done while capability checks are slow → the entry never appears, not even briefly.

cards.title: Onboarding checklist settings section
cards.user_does: Would open Settings and pick the onboarding checklist section.
cards.user_sees: The Setup Guide content embedded as a settings page.
rules: The guide keeps its own dialog and Help entry; only the settings section goes.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: setup-guide settings section removed by owner (table 1b); the guide keeps its own view. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Explore Kolux workflow tour
cards.user_does: Opens Help › 'Explore Kolux', moves through workflows with Continue or the left rail.
cards.user_sees: A large dialog describing itself as a short workflow-by-workflow tour: a rail of five workflows (workspaces, tasks, agents, workbench, review), each with an animated visual, a short caption, a docs link and Optional/Completed markers.
rules: Agents has sub-stops statuses, usage, orchestration; workbench has terminal, editor, browser; review has notes, PR view, ship.
Continue walks through sub-stops before the next workflow and uses the Ctrl/Cmd+Enter screen shortcut.
The rail answers ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home and End, clamped at both ends.
The Tasks stop shows unified task copy without leaving the walkthrough.
acceptance: Help › 'Explore Kolux' → dialog opens on workspaces with the rail visible.
On agents, Continue → statuses, usage, orchestration, then workbench.
Focus the rail and press End → last workflow selected.

cards.title: Explore Kolux completion requires a visit plus the real setup
cards.user_does: Visits workflows and sub-stops, sets things up, reopens the tour later.
cards.user_sees: Checkmarks only on stops the user has visited and, where setup is involved, actually configured; they survive reopening.
rules: Nothing is pre-checked because it is already configured; the user must visit it in the tour.
Tasks completes after visiting and a task source is connected; orchestration needs a visit and the orchestration skill detected; browser needs the browser-use skill.
Once complete, a stop or workflow stays complete even if detection later reports unavailable.
Visits are restored on reopen; unknown or duplicate ids are dropped.
Visit state lives in per-browser local storage, not the profile.
acceptance: Configure GitHub, open the tour → Tasks not checked until visited.
Complete review, reopen → still checked.

cards.title: Explore Kolux stops carry inline setup cards
cards.user_does: Changes a setting from inside a tour stop.
cards.user_sees: Per-stop setup: tasks shows provider rows; agent statuses shows a keep-PC-awake card; usage shows connected accounts; orchestration and browser stops show a skill setup card with an inline terminal; PR view shows GitHub; ship shows AI commit and PR text settings.
rules: Keep-awake turns on its automatic mode from off; either on mode can be turned off.
Usage counts as connected from managed accounts or from the provider's own default rate-limit data, even before live quota arrives.
Inline setup terminals are shorter when shown inside onboarding than in the tour.
acceptance: Keep-awake off → card switch turns on automatic mode.
Codex signed in outside Kolux → usage stop shows connected.

cards.title: Explore Kolux animated visuals respect visibility and platform
cards.user_does: Watches a tour stop, switches away and back.
cards.user_sees: Looping demos (workspace card rotation, workbench run queue, agent-status cycle, browser storyboard) that pause while hidden and resume where they left off; shortcut labels match the platform.
rules: Hidden demos pause and resume without skipping ahead.
Windows shows Ctrl-style shortcut copy in workbench and browser demos.
The browser demo keeps a fixed storyboard order and cycle length.
acceptance: Hide the window mid-rotation, return → same card continues.
On Windows → no Cmd symbols in the demos.

cards.title: Feature tile recordings and third-party names in tile captions
cards.user_does: Views the media tiles that feature the product.
cards.user_sees: Twelve animated tiles with poster frames, recorded before Kolux existed, with captions naming other tools (a terminal and an editor by brand, plus a list of agent CLIs).
rules: Each tile has an animation, a poster image and a recording-date record.
One tile shows remote workspaces, which belongs to the dropped remote area.
acceptance: Replacement tiles are recorded from Kolux RS itself and captions avoid other products' brands.
cards.decision: X: replace with the owner's own recordings of Kolux RS and own captions; drop the remote-workspaces tile with area 18.

cards.title: Startup feature tips: one tip per launch, in priority order
cards.user_does: Opens Kolux as an existing user.
cards.user_sees: At most one small tip dialog at launch: first the CLI tip, later the command-palette tip, then none.
rules: New tips come before older ones; seen tips and tips for features already done are skipped.
Never shown while onboarding is showing, and not later in that same session.
Waits until saved UI state is ready, settings and onboarding are loaded, no modal is open and the CLI install status is known.
The CLI tip is skipped when the CLI is unsupported or installed and on PATH; installed but off PATH still counts as not done.
If the CLI status read fails, the CLI is treated as installed.
A tip is marked seen the moment it is shown.
A tip already on screen stays open after it has been marked seen; it closes only when the user acts on it.
Seen tips are saved once; unknown tip ids from older data are dropped on load.
acceptance: Existing user without CLI → CLI tip on launch; relaunch → palette tip; relaunch → no tip.
First-time user → no tip during or after onboarding in that session.
cards.compat: Seen-tip ids are a data category the importer should carry.

cards.title: CLI feature tip installs the CLI and skills
cards.user_does: Clicks 'Install CLI & Skills' in the CLI tip.
cards.user_sees: A tip describing concrete things the CLI enables, an install action with an inline setup terminal, and a result of installed or needs attention.
rules: Result is installed only after clean registration; needs attention if install did not finish cleanly or the launcher is installed but not on PATH.
On Windows with a broken WSL runtime the setup runs on the host instead.
The tip's inline terminal behaves like the Setup Guide's CLI step: the command is typed at the prompt and runs only when the user presses Enter.
acceptance: Install succeeds and is on PATH → installed.
Installed but not on PATH → needs attention.

cards.title: Command palette tip with a one-shot demo
cards.user_does: Sees the palette tip and clicks 'Got it'.
cards.user_sees: A dialog with a tip badge, a title that includes the live palette shortcut as key chips, a short demo of typing in the palette that reveals a create-workspace row, and a note on how to rebind.
rules: Shortcut chips follow the user's binding; an unassigned binding falls back to the default; double-tap bindings show without plus signs.
The demo plays once and settles; with reduced motion it shows the end state with no timers.
The tip is a passive acknowledgement, not an action.
acceptance: Rebind the palette → tip title shows the new keys.
Reduced motion on → static end state.

cards.title: Voice dictation feature tip
cards.user_does: Would have been told about desktop voice dictation at launch.
cards.user_sees: Nothing now; the tip id is still accepted from older data but never saved or shown.
rules: Retired with desktop voice and dictation.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Contextual tour overlay: callouts with Back, Next, Skip and Done
cards.user_does: Follows a tour that appears next to a real control.
cards.user_sees: A floating panel anchored to the target with step copy, progress dots and a step label, Back/Next/Skip buttons, Done on the last step, and an optional pulsing ring on the target.
rules: Single-step tours show no step label; Back is hidden on the first visible step.
Some steps replace Next with an action button, or hide it when the real control is the call to action.
Escape acts as Skip before page shortcuts see it; if the panel is gone, Escape does nothing.
The panel follows its target as layout changes and re-measures cheaply; it works inside dialogs and side sheets.
Steps whose target is missing are skipped and progress counts only visible steps.
Tour copy is localized.
While the app window is hidden the panel stops its periodic re-measure, and re-measures as soon as the window is visible again.
A target that keeps moving for a few frames, or moves without any layout event, is still followed.
The panel sits on the step's preferred side of its target with an arrow pointing at it; when no side has room it stays inside the window or dialog, overlapping the target if it must.
acceptance: Press Escape during a tour → tour ends as skipped and is not shown again.
Resize the window → panel stays attached to its target.

cards.title: Contextual tours show once, only for new profiles, when the target is ready
cards.user_does: Visits a feature for the first time.
cards.user_sees: A tour the first time only, if this profile started with onboarding; explicit buttons can replay a tour at any time.
rules: Auto-tour eligibility is decided once: profiles that saw onboarding at first load are eligible; existing profiles never get automatic tours.
No tour until onboarding has loaded, and none while it shows.
A tour starts only after saved seen-ids load and its first target is visible and measurable; hidden copies are passed over; if measurement fails the tour does not start and is not marked seen.
No tour starts over a confirmation dialog; only the workspace-creation tour may run over its own composer.
Skipping or finishing marks the tour seen once; stale dismissals for another tour are ignored.
If the feature that owns a tour turns off, the tour is suppressed unless it was intentionally detached.
A forced request from a button retries until the target appears, stops if another tour starts or the user moves away, and can wait for another tour to clear.
A tour waiting for its first target gives up after a capped number of tries (about 20) instead of watching forever.

At most one tour starts on its own per app session; a tour cancelled before it ever appeared frees that slot, one that already appeared keeps it used. A replay button ignores both the per-session limit and the seen list.
acceptance: Existing profile updates → no automatic tours.
New profile opens the browser pane → browser tour once; second visit → none.
Click a replay button with tours exhausted → tour runs.
Enable a tour whose target never renders → after the retry cap nothing is still watching and no tour appears.
Meet two surfaces with unseen tours in one session → only the first tour appears on its own; the second waits for the next launch, but its replay button still opens it now.
cards.compat: Seen tour ids and auto-tour eligibility are a data category the importer should carry.

cards.title: Contextual tour catalogue
cards.user_does: Meets each surface for the first time.
cards.user_sees: Short tours for: the board (plan, move through lanes to done); running agents in parallel (split a pane, then start another task); the browser pane (grab, annotate, keep logged in by importing cookies); tasks (source, filter, start from a row); automations (create, then results); the floating workspace (works across all projects, scratchpad); workspace creation (pick project, name or reuse work, choose agent); and the post-onboarding grid tour.
rules: The parallel-agents tour advances from the split step when the split command runs, opens the sidebar if the create button is hidden, and cancels if that button is absent.
The browser cookie step waits until its menu row can be measured, falling back from a hint button to the overflow menu row.
The floating workspace tour falls back to the panel surface when its list is empty.
The workspace-creation tour hands off into the composer; enabling first-message auto-naming clears a generated name, disabling it leaves the name.
The parallel-agents tour offers itself only on an active workspace terminal tab, and only to people who have never split a pane.

cards.title: GitHub star prompt: when it appears
cards.user_does: Uses Kolux: launches many agents, gets a finished result, or finishes onboarding.
cards.user_sees: A card asking for a GitHub star after enough agents, after a finished task, or a toast right after onboarding completes.
rules: Threshold: 35 agents launched since the baseline taken for the current app version; every update resets the baseline unless the user already completed the prompt.
'Later' starts a three-day cooldown and doubles the next threshold.
A finished-task moment fires once per app version: after a non-interrupted completion of a prompted session, once other live agents and typing have been quiet for about a second.
The onboarding-completed prompt uses a toast and replaces any visible threshold card; if a check is in flight it queues behind it.
If the user has already starred, nothing shows and a visible card is hidden.
Prompts are never shown while a cooldown is active, after completion, or when no window can receive them; a forced show bypasses the cooldown.
A finished-task moment that arrives during a cooldown is used up for that app version and does not show later in it; one that finds no window to show in is not used up.
A dismissal counts only while a prompt is showing and only once per prompt: stray or repeated dismissals neither restart the cooldown nor double the threshold again.
acceptance: Launch 35 agents in a new version → card shows.
Click 'Later' → nothing for three days, then only after 70 more agents.
Finish onboarding → star toast appears.
cards.compat: Star-prompt state (baseline, next threshold, cooldown, completed) is a data category the importer should carry.

cards.title: GitHub star prompt: starring and its states
cards.user_does: Clicks 'Star on GitHub', 'Later' or 'Dismiss' in the card or toast; or uses the star button in Settings General or the landing screen.
cards.user_sees: The star is applied directly through the user's GitHub sign-in, with a busy state and then a thank-you; if direct starring is not possible, an 'Open GitHub' button opens the repo page instead.
rules: Success is confirmed only after the direct star succeeds.
If the star state cannot be checked, the browser fallback is offered; a failed direct star switches to the fallback.
While busy, Dismiss and closing are disabled; duplicate in-flight stars are ignored and a thrown attempt can be retried.
Replacing or hiding the toast is not counted as the user dismissing it.
The landing-screen star updates optimistically.
If the user dismisses while a direct star is still running and it then fails, the cooldown stands and the prompt does not come back.
acceptance: Signed in to GitHub → 'Star on GitHub' → busy → thank-you.
Not signed in → 'Open GitHub' opens the repo in the browser.

cards.title: Kolux remembers locally which features each profile has used
cards.user_does: Uses features in the normal course of work: opens the board, the palette, the browser pane, Tasks, Automations, splits a pane, creates a workspace, sets up a skill, and so on.
cards.user_sees: Nothing directly; guidance adapts. Setup steps tick off from real use, tours aimed at a feature stop offering themselves once that feature is already familiar, and one-off hints reach only people who used the old location of a moved control.
rules: For a fixed list of about forty features, the profile keeps the time of first use and a running count of uses.
Nothing is recorded until saved interface state has loaded; earlier uses are not counted.
Counts only grow; when saves finish out of order the newest count wins.
On load, records for unknown features and malformed records are dropped silently.
Opening a surface that has a tour counts as using that feature.
Has-used checks feed: the browser setup step, the legacy split-pane setup credit, the parallel-agents tour gate, the moved-control hint, and tips a feature use makes pointless.
The record stays on the machine; its usage-band telemetry is compiled off.
acceptance: Fresh profile: view a non-blank page in the browser pane → the Setup Guide browser step ticks, and stays ticked after a restart.
Split a terminal pane once, then open a new workspace → the parallel-agents tour does not start.
Add an unknown feature name to the saved record → it is ignored on load and nothing errors.
